procedure: Project the validated independent source contract from the immutable successor audit; retain its full source evidence, conventions and ambiguities in the sealed output.

payload.source_label: Contaminant mass conservation with flux f(q) = ubar q yields the advection equation

contract.statement: For a contaminant carried through a one-dimensional pipe by fluid with constant velocity ū, conservation of total contaminant mass gives the density advection equation q_t + ūq_x = 0, and the associated flux is exactly f(q) = ūq. This combines the entire selected third sentence after (1.10) on printed page 4 with its explicit reference to (1.2) on printed page 1. The surrounding integral law describes mass change through endpoint fluxes; the source separately qualifies passage to a classical differential equation by sufficient smoothness (printed page 4, (1.10) and Section 1.1.2).
assumptions: A contaminant is advected with fluid flowing through a one-dimensional pipe at constant velocity ū. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, paragraph introducing (1.2); raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, selected sentence's reference to flow down the pipe.]

The total mass of contaminant is conserved as it flows down the pipe. This is the physical premise from which the selected sentence says the equation is derived. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, selected third sentence after (1.10).]

The claim is a physical modeling example within the integral-form discussion, rather than a separately quantified theorem. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, Section 1.1.1, selected sentence beginning 'For example'.]

Conservation allows the mass in a fixed spatial interval to change through endpoint fluxes; it does not assert that every such interval has constant mass. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, (1.10) and first sentence after it.]

For a classical differential derivation from integral balance, the source requires q and f(q) to be sufficiently smooth, without specifying an exact regularity class here. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, opening sentence of Section 1.1.2.]
quantifiers: Inherited setting: x ∈ ℝ is the spatial coordinate and t ∈ ℝ is time; the chapter introduces q on ℝ × ℝ. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, text following (1.1).]

Inherited scalar field: q(x,t) ∈ ℝ represents contaminant concentration or density in the one-dimensional pipe. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, scalar specialization and paragraph introducing (1.2).]

Inherited parameter: ū is the constant real fluid velocity appearing in the scalar advection equation. No sign or nonzero restriction is stated. [Raw PDF page 23, printed page 1, scalar real-coefficient discussion and paragraph introducing (1.2).]

The scalar flux f is specified by f(r) = ūr, with r used here to distinguish a scalar state from the field q(x,t). The source writes this identity as f(q) = ūq without an explicit quantifier. [Raw PDF page 26, printed page 4, selected third sentence after (1.10).]
